control.description: Upstream generate_sql unchanged: by default (allow_llm_to_see_data=False) query results are never put into the prompt; the caller must opt in.

vulnerable.description: Controlled mutation of the control: the default becomes allow_llm_to_see_data=True, so any caller that relies on the default sends rows from the database to the LLM provider (and to the log). Only the signature line changes.

excerpts.symbol: fix_sql endpoint (calls generate_sql with the default)

data_flow.source: Rows returned by the model-requested intermediate SQL query (customer data in the harness).
data_flow.sink: Prompt sent to the external LLM provider through submit_prompt (and printed by log).

validation.summary: Stubbed retrieval, database and model. When the simulated model asks for intermediate SQL, a dummy customer email reaches the second prompt only in the vulnerable version; the control returns upstream's refusal message.

assumptions: The database holds personal or confidential data that must not leave the organisation.
The LLM is an external provider (Vanna's typical setup).
limitations: No live LLM inference is run.
If the owner explicitly opts in, sending data is intended; the label concerns the unsafe default only.
Retrieval, prompt building and SQL extraction are stubbed.
